newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money up after long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money up after long weekend.

text.p: *Banks see slide in Treasury bill rates
Manila overnight money rose to an average of 11.3125 percent on Tuesday from 11.28125 after banks covered their long weekend positions, traders said. Monday was a holiday.
Done rates were from 11.5 to 11.28125 percent, with 39 lenders and 23 borrowers. Volume expanded to 22.81 billion pesos from 11.87 billion.
On the secondary market, some banks were buying one-year T-bills in anticipation of a slide in Treasury bill rates in the auction later today.
The expected lower T-bill rates were triggered by the 0.25 percentage-point cut in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate last Thursday.
Overall, however, there was little activity in the market.
"Some are quite cautious," a dealer said. "Banks are not very aggressive in buying. They don't want to place all their bullets."
Some banks believe T-bill rates may stay at current levels until the May 20 meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee which will decided whether to change rates, traders said.
They also think the Central Bank may just maintain its overnight borrowing rate at 11.25 percent if there are no substantial dollar inflows.
A Reuter poll of five financial institutions gave bid rates of 11.40 to 11.80 percent on the one-year bills.
